Interpreted as systemic allopurinol hypersensitivity: severe skin injury, with hepatic and renal injury each occurring in roughly half or more.
Inherited junctional skin blistering; enamel hypoplasia affecting teeth is characteristic and common (>30%) in junctional EB.
Progressive skeletal muscular dystrophy; motor delay reflects weakness. Cardiopulmonary abnormalities are very rare.
Progressive tubulointerstitial kidney disease, childhood hypoproliferative anemia and hyperuricemia are defining features.
Acromelic skeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; cognitive impairment and eyelid ptosis each occur in 30-79%. Cosmetic skin and ear features excluded.
Permanent cerebral motor-system injury causes unilateral spastic weakness.
Malignancy of precursor lymphoid blood cells; lymphoma also receives the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Umbrella group of inherited reticulate skin pigmentation disorders.

Bone is the dominant site occupied by metastatic prostate carcinoma, affecting roughly 80-90%; the prostatic origin itself has no axis.
Adult-onset ataxia and peripheral neuropathy define the phenotype; supplied ancestry identifies an inborn metabolic/DNA-repair disorder.
Inward rotation of the eyelid margin is an ocular adnexal disorder.
Tumor arises in the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the anatomical axes; no other affected site is specified.
Deficient gonadotropin secretion defines the endocrine disease; anosmia is a defining Kallmann feature and occurred in 4/4 annotated patients.
Hair dysplasia/alopecia and defective dental enamel jointly define the syndrome; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Scaly inflammation is confined to skin; nonspecific inflammation does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Maternal alloantibodies destroy fetal/neonatal platelets. Intracranial hemorrhage is a minority complication.
Rhabdomyosarcoma is a malignant tumor with skeletal-muscle differentiation; no additional organ site is specified.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing impairment; hearing loss occurred in 10/10 annotated patients.
Inherited disruption of polyamine metabolism; heterogeneous subtypes do not establish another commonly damaged organ across the group.
A peripheral nerve pain disorder; no additional organ damage is intrinsic to the umbrella concept.
Renal artery stenosis and resulting systemic hypertension are vascular disease; renal parenchymal damage is not required.
Usually chronic infection-associated pelvic inflammatory disease; fallopian tubes themselves are outside the anatomical axes.
